summary:
SONORA turns NASA's Earth visualizations into music that anyone can hear, explore and understand without needing to see them. It answers The Earth Information Jukebox challenge with a web jukebox of 24 NASA visualizations from the Earth Information Center (Scientific Visualization Studio) and NASA Earth Observatory Global Maps: temperature anomalies, El Niño 2026, aerosols, CO₂, methane, smoke, rainfall, vegetation and more. Each visualization is analyzed frame by frame; its four dominant color families become melody, rhythm, bass and harmony, so rising temperatures literally sound higher. Users can also sonify their own images and videos, Peru's biomes (a neural network trained on NASA data) and climate trends from NASA POWER and Giovanni.
SONORA was designed first for blind and low-vision people: a voice assistant and hands-free mode, a full page reader, spoken step-by-step descriptions, keyboard navigation, haptic feedback, high contrast and downloadable transcripts. Every piece can be downloaded as audio or as video with sound, building a shareable playlist of our planet. It matters because Earth science should be accessible to everyone, through every sense.
details:
SONORA is an accessible web application that transforms Earth observation imagery into music in real time.

  • NASA Jukebox (EIC): 24 curated visualizations (NASA SVS 5603, 5688, 5687, 5572, 5436, 5554, 5624, 5616, 5669, and 15 global maps from NASA Earth Observatory). Each is stored as a lightweight WebP sprite sheet (48 frames, approximately 1 MB), enabling near-instant loading and efficient deployment on lightweight hosting infrastructure.
  • Your Own Files: Upload any image or video and process it locally in your browser.
  • Peruvian Biomes: A neural network trained on NASA satellite data classifies each grid cell, allowing users to explore changes year by year from 2001 to 2024.
  • Peruvian Climate: Climate trends from NASA POWER and Giovanni are analyzed using a neural network optimized with NSGA-II to identify which variables are actually changing. Each variable is then translated into a musical instrument.
  • Explore the Entire Planet: Select any region on a NASA GIBS map and listen to its corresponding soundscape.

HOW IT WORKS

SONORA samples video frames and groups image pixels into four color families using k-means clustering or NASA's official color scale. These groups are mapped to melody, rhythm, bass, and harmony through a temporal or west-to-east scanning process.

Intensity controls pitch and volume, while isolated bright spots—such as wildfires or city lights—become distinctive sonic accents.

A multi-objective optimizer balances scientific fidelity with musicality, allowing users to adjust the balance between accurate data representation and artistic expression.

ACCESSIBILITY

Designed for blind and low-vision users.

  • Voice Assistant with Hands-Free Mode: Users can issue commands such as "Play the Sahara," "Where is the most smoke?", "Go to Accessibility," or "Play number three."
  • Full-Page Screen Reader and Voice Navigation: Voice-based navigation through every section and interactive control.
  • Comprehensive Accessibility Features: Spoken descriptions of each step, ARIA live regions, full keyboard control, haptic feedback on Android, high-contrast mode, large text, and downloadable transcripts.
  • Automatic Language Detection: English and Spanish interfaces based on the browser's language settings.
  • Export Options: Download each generated composition as an audio file or as a video with synchronized sound.

TECHNOLOGIES AND TOOLS

Backend and Frontend: C# / .NET 10, ASP.NET Core, and Blazor WebAssembly.

Artificial Intelligence and Neural Networks: Hba.NeuralNet, using Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) neural networks for Peruvian biome classification and climate trend analysis.

Evolutionary Optimization: HBA.Evolutivo, implementing genetic algorithms and NSGA-II for multi-objective optimization of sonification mappings and neural network hyperparameters.

Audio, Mapping, and Accessibility: JavaScript, Tone.js for audio synthesis, Leaflet for interactive maps, Web Speech API for speech synthesis and recognition, and MediaRecorder for multimedia recording.

Geospatial and Scientific Data Sources: OpenStreetMap, NASA GIBS, NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS), NASA Earth Observatory, NASA POWER, and data accessed through NASA Giovanni.

CREATIVITY AND IMPACT

SONORA allows people to hear climate change.

Warming anomalies rise in pitch, El Niño intensifies across the Pacific Ocean, and atmospheric smoke and dust transform into rhythm.

By turning scientific data into immersive musical experiences, SONORA makes NASA's Earth science more accessible to blind and low-vision communities, classrooms, museums, and the general public.

The platform creates a shared sonic playlist of our planet, connecting science, technology, music, and accessibility.

BENEFITS OF THE PROJECT

  • Accessibility by Design: SONORA lowers barriers for blind and low-vision users through a voice assistant with hands-free mode, full-page screen reader and voice navigation, ARIA live regions, full keyboard control, haptic feedback on Android, high-contrast mode, large text, and downloadable transcripts.
  • Real-Time, Lightweight Experience: Curated NASA visualizations are stored as lightweight WebP sprite sheets (48 frames, approximately 1 MB), enabling near-instant loading and efficient deployment on lightweight hosting infrastructure.
  • Local and Private Processing: Users can upload any image or video and process it locally in the browser, supporting efficient use without relying on server-side processing.
  • Scientific Fidelity with Adjustable Musicality: A multi-objective optimizer balances accurate data representation with artistic expression, allowing users to adjust sonification mappings while preserving the scientific signal.
  • Hearing Climate and Earth Processes: Warming anomalies rise in pitch, El Niño intensifies across the Pacific Ocean, and atmospheric smoke and dust transform into rhythm, making climate change and Earth observation data audible and immersive.
  • AI-Supported Scientific Exploration: Multilayer Perceptron neural networks classify Peruvian biomes and analyze climate trends, while NSGA-II evolutionary optimization improves sonification mappings and neural network hyperparameters.
  • Education, Public Engagement, and Inclusion: SONORA makes NASA Earth science more accessible to blind and low-vision communities, classrooms, museums, and the general public, creating a shared sonic playlist of our planet that connects science, technology, music, and accessibility.
  • Multilingual and Shareable Outputs: Automatic English and Spanish interfaces based on browser language settings, plus export options for audio files or video with synchronized sound, support broader reach and reuse.
  • Scalable Exploration: Users can explore Peruvian biomes year by year from 2001 to 2024, analyze Peruvian climate trends, and select any region on a NASA GIBS map to listen to its corresponding soundscape.
